Now let me decide. The dev compose is the documented method 2. I'll fix the two bugs and the init.sh bug, then bring up the dev stack and verify. This is the cleanest path. Let me apply fixes.

Actually, let me reconsider whether to modify repo files. The task is to install the software. Fixing bugs is reasonable necessary action. But modifying repo files could be considered beyond "installation". However, these are genuine blockers. The dev compose path is documented. Let me fix them.

Fix 1: init.sh - guard REVOKEs (won't fail if tables missing). Actually the REVOKE on nonexistent table errors. Better: only revoke if table exists. Or wrap in DO block checking to_regclass.

Fix 2: dev compose nginx mount.

Fix 3: dev compose qgis heredoc -> use printf.

Let me apply.

action.command:
cd /workspace/deployment && python3 - <<'PY'
import re
p='postgres/init.sh'
s=open(p).read()
old="""        -- Revoke access on model and route permissions
        REVOKE ALL ON model_permission FROM "$QGIS_DB_USER";
        REVOKE ALL ON route_permission FROM "$QGIS_DB_USER";"""
new="""        -- Revoke access on model and route permissions (tables are created
        -- later by Django migrations, so tolerate their absence on first init)
        DO \\$\\$
        BEGIN
            IF to_regclass('public.model_permission') IS NOT NULL THEN
                EXECUTE 'REVOKE ALL ON model_permission FROM ' || quote_ident('$QGIS_DB_USER');
            END IF;
            IF to_regclass('public.route_permission') IS NOT NULL THEN
                EXECUTE 'REVOKE ALL ON route_permission FROM ' || quote_ident('$QGIS_DB_USER');
            END IF;
        END
        \\$\\$;"""
assert old in s, "old block not found"
s=s.replace(old,new)
open(p,'w').write(s)
print("patched init.sh")
PY
sed -n '60,80p' postgres/init.sh
